provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after 'ea'; the 1962 sets one; 1862 conclusion is the short cue 'Per Dominum.'; the 1962 prints 'iustitiae'; the project orthography and the 1862 print 'justitiae'. Corroboration: none available: neither the 1570 nor the 1604 yields this collect in usable OCR (the 1570's leaves at 44300-44420 are largely illegible and the 1604 returns nothing for 'errantibus', 'redire iustiti', 'respuere' or 'sectari'). Recorded limitation: LETTERFORM INFERRED. The 1862 layer reads 'guae huic inimica' at line 44099 for 'quae'; the same word is printed legibly one line later in the same sentence ('et ea quae sunt apta' at 44100), which is the only support I have, since no independent public-domain witness could be read for this prayer. Recorded rather than repaired.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui errantibus, ut in viam possint redire justitiae, veritatis tuae
lumen ostendis: da cunctis, qui christiana professione censentur, et illa
respuere, quae huic inimica sunt nomini; et ea, quae sunt apta, sectari. Per
Dominum nostrum.
